newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says spousal maintenance may be in lump sum payment.
newsitem.headline: Court says spousal maintenance may be in lump sum payment.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday court awarded spousal maintenance, whether received in a lump sum or in multiple payments, must be enforced between member states.

The court noted that although the Brussels Convention on the Enforcement of Civil Judgments does not require another state's court to enforce an evaluation of marital property rights, it does cover spousal maintenance awards.

In this case, the British High Court awarded a lump sum spousal maintenance. When the beneficiary of that award tried to enforce the judgment in the Netherlands, the payor spouse challenged his ex-wife's right to enforce the award.

"If the award is designed to enable one spouse to provide for himself or herself...the decision is concerned with maintenance...if the award is solely concerned with dividing property...it will not be enforceable under the Brussels Convention," the court said.

The court in this ruling made it clear to the Dutch District Court in Amsterdam that the judgment from the British court awarding spousal maintenance in a lump sum must be enforced in the Netherlands.
Reference from the District Court, Amsterdam for a preliminary ruling in the case between
on the interpretation of article 1 of the Brussels Convention (OJ 1978 L 304, p. 77)

A decision rendered in divorce proceedings ordering payment of a lump sum and transfer of ownership in certain property by one party to his or her former spouse must be regarded as relating to maintenance and therefore as falling within the scope of the Brussels Convention on Jurisdiction, as amended, if its purpose is to ensure the former spouse's mainenance. The fact that in its decision the court of origin disregarded a marriage contract is of no account in this regard.
